name: Moyamoya Angiopathy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Research Committee on Spontaneous Occlusion of the Circle of Willis Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Bilateral stenosis or occlusion of the terminal portion of the internal carotid arteries and proximal portions of the anterior and middle cerebral arteries
Presence of abnormal vascular networks (moyamoya vessels) at the base of the brain on angiography
Exclusion of other causes of intracranial arterial stenosis such as atherosclerosis, autoimmune disease, or radiation-induced vasculopathy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Bilateral stenosis or occlusion of the terminal internal carotid arteries with presence of moyamoya vessels on angiography and exclusion of secondary causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis can be confirmed by cerebral angiography or magnetic resonance angiography (MRA).

pathognomonic.symptomName: Ischemic stroke in the anterior circulation
Cerebral hemorrhage due to fragile collateral vessels

common.symptomName: Cognitive impairment or developmental delay in pediatric patients

laboratory: Generally nonspecific; routine labs usually normal
Exclusion of autoimmune markers to rule out secondary causes
imaging: Cerebral angiography showing stenosis/occlusion of terminal internal carotid arteries with 'puff of smoke' collateral vessels
Magnetic resonance angiography (MRA) demonstrating characteristic vascular changes
MRI brain showing ischemic or hemorrhagic lesions in affected territories
genetic: RNF213 gene mutation (especially in East Asian populations) associated with familial cases
other: Electroencephalogram (EEG) may show focal slowing or epileptiform discharges in seizure patients

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of vascular risk factors (hypertension, diabetes, hyperlipidemia)
Absence of characteristic moyamoya collateral vessels on angiography
Segmental vessel wall inflammation on imaging or biopsy

redFlags: Recurrent transient ischemic attacks in a child or young adult
Intracranial hemorrhage with no obvious cause
references: Research Committee on Spontaneous Occlusion of the Circle of Willis (Moyamoya Disease). Guidelines for diagnosis and treatment of Moyamoya disease. Neurol Med Chir (Tokyo). 2012.
Scott RM, Smith ER. Moyamoya disease and Moyamoya syndrome. N Engl J Med. 2009.
Kamada F, et al. A genome-wide association study identifies RNF213 as the first Moyamoya disease gene. J Hum Genet. 2011.
